title: Planning the team's next steps
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender a falar de planos e decisões já tomadas usando 'going to'. Isso é essencial em Gestão de Pessoas na Delta Ducon para anunciar contratações, treinamentos e reuniões que já estão definidos com a sua equipe.
intro: In People Management, we talk about the future every day. We plan interviews, training sessions and one-to-one meetings with our team.
Today we use 'going to' to share plans that are already decided. It is the perfect way to tell your colleagues what will happen next at Delta Ducon.
introAudio: Hi, I am Paula from HR. This week I am going to interview two engineers and plan a new training. Let us learn how to talk about our team plans.
vocab: Our team is going to grow this year.
We are going to hire a new engineer.
The training is going to start on Monday.
The meeting is going to be short today.
I am going to check the schedule with my manager.
The onboarding is going to help her feel welcome.
practice: We are going to ______ two new technicians this month.
hire
The safety ______ is going to run every Friday.
training
Our ______ is going to grow after the new contract.
team
I am going to send the ______ to everyone tomorrow.
schedule
The 1:1 ______ is going to happen at three o'clock.
meeting
Her ______ is going to last one week at the Diadema factory.
onboarding
They are going to ______ a project manager for the mining client.
hire
The whole ______ is going to join the review call.
team

audio.title: Plans for the new engineer
audio.text: Next week we are going to welcome a new engineer to the emissions team. On Monday, she is going to meet her manager and see the Diadema factory. We are going to give her a full onboarding plan. In the afternoon, the team is going to have a short meeting to share the schedule. I am going to be her mentor for the first month. Everyone is going to help her feel at home.

readAloud: We are going to hire a new engineer next month.
I am going to run the training on Friday.
The team is going to meet at three o'clock.
She is going to lead the onboarding.
They are going to review the schedule tomorrow.
fill: We are ___ to hire a new technician.
I ___ going to lead the training.
She is going ___ meet her manager on Monday.
They ___ going to review the schedule.
The team is going ___ grow this year.
He ___ going to start the onboarding today.
We are going ___ have a short meeting.
I am ___ to send the plan tonight.
qa: What are you going to do this week?
I am going to interview two candidates.
Who is going to lead the training?
Paula is going to lead the training.
When is the team going to meet?
The team is going to meet on Monday.
Are you going to hire a new engineer?
Yes, we are going to hire one next month.
How are you going to help the new colleague?
I am going to be her mentor.
sentences: We are going to hire two new engineers this year.
I am going to lead the onboarding next week.
The team is going to meet every Monday.
She is going to run the safety training.
They are going to review the schedule tomorrow.
We are going to welcome the new colleague on Monday.
I am going to prepare the 1:1 meeting.
The team is going to grow after the new contract.
grammarPoint: Use 'going to' para planos e decisões já tomados sobre o futuro. Estrutura: am/is/are + going to + verbo. I am going to hire a new engineer. — Eu vou contratar um novo engenheiro. We are going to start the training. — Nós vamos começar o treinamento.
deepDive: Escolha am, is ou are conforme o sujeito: I am, he/she/it is, we/you/they are. Depois de 'going to' vem sempre o verbo na forma base (sem -s, sem -ed). Dica: use 'going to' quando o plano já está decidido, não apenas imaginado.
examples: I am going to interview the candidate.
Eu vou entrevistar o candidato.
We are going to hire a new manager.
Nós vamos contratar um novo gerente.
She is going to lead the training.
Ela vai conduzir o treinamento.
They are going to join the team next month.
Eles vão entrar na equipe no próximo mês.
He is going to start his onboarding on Monday.
Ele vai começar a integração na segunda.
I am going to send the schedule today.
Eu vou enviar a agenda hoje.
We are going to have a 1:1 meeting.
Nós vamos ter uma reunião individual.
The team is going to grow this year.
A equipe vai crescer este ano.
You are going to enjoy the new role.
Você vai gostar da nova função.
I am going to give her feedback tomorrow.
Eu vou dar o feedback a ela amanhã.
mistakes: I going to hire a new engineer.
I am going to hire a new engineer.
Não esqueça o verbo to be antes de 'going to'.
We are going to hired a manager.
We are going to hire a manager.
Depois de 'going to' o verbo fica na forma base.
She is go to lead the training.
She is going to lead the training.
Use 'going to', não 'go to'.
They is going to meet on Monday.
They are going to meet on Monday.
Com they usamos are, não is.
I am going hire a technician.
I am going to hire a technician.
Não esqueça o 'to' entre going e o verbo.
quick: I ___ going to lead the meeting.
We are ___ to hire a technician.
She is going ___ start on Monday.
They ___ going to review the plan.
He is going ___ join the team.

celebrate.en: Well done. You can now share your team's plans with confidence — a key skill for any people manager.
celebrate.pt: Muito bem. Agora você sabe compartilhar os planos da sua equipe com confiança — uma habilidade essencial para quem gere pessoas.

title: Making predictions and offers to your team
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender a usar 'will' para fazer previsões e oferecer ajuda. Em Gestão de Pessoas na Delta Ducon, isso serve para tranquilizar a equipe, prometer apoio e antecipar como um projeto ou um novo colaborador vão se sair.
intro: Sometimes we do not have a fixed plan — we simply predict the future or offer help in the moment. For that we use 'will'.
As a people manager at Delta Ducon, you will say things like 'I will help you' or 'The new engineer will do well'. Let us practise these useful phrases.
introAudio: Hello, I am Bruno from People Management. I think the new hire will do great, and I will help her every step of the way. Let us learn how to use will.
vocab: I will support you during your first week.
The candidate will start next Monday.
I will give you feedback after the meeting.
The team will reach its goal this quarter.
A mentor will guide the new technician.
Her performance will improve with training.
practice: I will give you clear ______ after the review.
feedback
The new ______ will start at the Uberlândia site.
candidate
A senior engineer will act as her ______.
mentor
I will ______ you if the project gets difficult.
support
The team will reach its ______ for this quarter.
goal
With training, his ______ will get even better.
performance
Do not worry — I will ______ you during the audit.
support
We think the ______ will accept our offer.
candidate

audio.title: You will do great
audio.text: Do not worry about your first month here. You will meet your team on Monday, and they will help you learn our processes. I will be your mentor, so I will answer all your questions. I think you will enjoy the work at Delta Ducon. Your performance will grow every week. If you need anything, I will support you right away.

readAloud: I will support you during the audit.
The new candidate will start next week.
I will give you feedback tomorrow.
The team will reach its goal.
Do not worry, I will help you.
fill: I ___ support you during your first week.
We ___ reach our goal this quarter.
I ___ give you feedback after the meeting.
A mentor ___ guide the new engineer.
Do not worry, I ___ help you.
They ___ join the team next month.
qa: Will you help me with the report?
Yes, I will help you with it.
When will the new candidate start?
The candidate will start next Monday.
Do you think the team will reach the goal?
Yes, I think the team will reach it.
Who will be my mentor?
Bruno will be your mentor.
Will you give me feedback?
Yes, I will give you feedback tomorrow.
sentences: I will support you during your first week.
The new candidate will start on Monday.
I will give you honest feedback.
The team will reach its goal this quarter.
A mentor will guide the new engineer.
I think you will enjoy this role.
Do not worry, I will help you.
Her performance will improve with training.
grammarPoint: Use 'will' + verbo base para previsões ('acho que vai acontecer') e ofertas ('eu ajudo'). I will help you. — Eu vou te ajudar / eu ajudo. The team will reach its goal. — A equipe vai atingir a meta.
deepDive: 'Will' é igual para todos os sujeitos: I will, she will, they will. Depois dele vem o verbo na forma base (will help, will start). Dica: use 'going to' para planos já combinados e 'will' para previsões e ofertas feitas na hora.
examples: I will support you during the audit.
Eu vou te apoiar durante a auditoria.
The candidate will start next week.
O candidato vai começar na próxima semana.
I will give you feedback tomorrow.
Eu vou te dar um retorno amanhã.
The team will reach its goal.
A equipe vai atingir a meta.
A mentor will guide the new hire.
Um mentor vai orientar o novo contratado.
You will enjoy this role.
Você vai gostar desta função.
Her performance will improve.
O desempenho dela vai melhorar.
I will answer all your questions.
Eu vou responder a todas as suas perguntas.
We will hire two more engineers.
Nós vamos contratar mais dois engenheiros.
They will help you learn the process.
Eles vão te ajudar a aprender o processo.
mistakes: I will to help you.
I will help you.
Depois de 'will' não se usa 'to'.
She will helps the team.
She will help the team.
Depois de 'will' o verbo fica na forma base, sem -s.
The team will reaches its goal.
The team will reach its goal.
Não acrescente -es após will.
I will supported you.
I will support you.
Use o verbo base após will, não no passado.
Will you to give feedback?
Will you give feedback?
Em perguntas, também não use 'to' depois de will.
quick: I ___ support you during the audit.

celebrate.en: Excellent work. Offering support and sharing a positive outlook builds trust — and now you can do both in English.
celebrate.pt: Excelente trabalho. Oferecer apoio e transmitir confiança fortalece a equipe — e agora você faz as duas coisas em inglês.

title: Giving advice in one-to-one meetings
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender a dar conselhos usando 'should' e 'shouldn't'. Em Gestão de Pessoas na Delta Ducon, isso é fundamental para orientar a equipe em feedbacks, reuniões 1:1 e no desenvolvimento profissional de cada colaborador.
intro: A good people manager gives clear, kind advice. In one-to-one meetings, you help each person grow.
Today we use 'should' for good advice and 'shouldn't' for things to avoid. These words make your feedback helpful and respectful at Delta Ducon.
introAudio: Hi, I am Carla from People Management. In our 1:1 meetings, I often say what you should do and what you should not do. Let us learn to give advice in English.
vocab: I have some advice for your development.
You should listen to your colleagues.
You should set your priorities each morning.
You shouldn't hide a mistake from your manager.
You should plan your career with your leader.
practice: You should ask for ______ when you feel unsure.
advice
You should always meet the ______ for each report.
deadline
You should help a new ______ on the emissions team.
colleague
Safety should be your first ______ at the factory.
priority
You shouldn't repeat the same ______ twice.
mistake
You should think about your ______ at Delta Ducon.
career
A manager should give honest ______ in a kind way.
advice
You shouldn't miss an important ______ without warning.
deadline

audio.title: Advice for a strong start
audio.text: In your first months, you should ask many questions. You should listen to your colleagues and learn the safety rules. You shouldn't be afraid to make a mistake, but you should tell your manager about it. You should set clear priorities every morning. You shouldn't work alone when a task is difficult. If you follow this advice, you should grow fast at Delta Ducon.

readAloud: You should ask for help when you need it.
You shouldn't hide a mistake.
You should respect every deadline.
You shouldn't work alone on a hard task.
You should plan your career with your manager.
fill: You ___ hide a mistake from your manager.
You ___ ask for advice when you are unsure.
You ___ set clear priorities each morning.
You ___ speak badly about a colleague.
qa: What should I do on my first day?
You should meet the team and ask questions.
Should I tell my manager about a mistake?
Yes, you should tell your manager.
What shouldn't I do in a meeting?
You shouldn't interrupt your colleagues.
Should I set priorities every day?
Yes, you should set them every morning.
How should I give feedback?
You should give it in a clear and kind way.
sentences: You should ask for help when you need it.
You shouldn't hide a mistake.
You should respect every deadline.
You shouldn't miss an important meeting.
A manager should give honest feedback.
You should set clear priorities.
You shouldn't work alone on a hard task.
You should plan your career with your leader.
grammarPoint: Use 'should' + verbo base para dar bons conselhos e 'shouldn't' (should not) para dizer o que evitar. You should ask for help. — Você deveria pedir ajuda. You shouldn't hide a mistake. — Você não deveria esconder um erro.
deepDive: 'Should' e 'shouldn't' são iguais para todos os sujeitos (I, you, he, she, they) e vêm sempre com o verbo na forma base, sem 'to'. Dica: 'should' suaviza o conselho e soa mais respeitoso do que 'must' em um feedback.
examples: You should ask for advice.
Você deveria pedir conselho.
You shouldn't hide a mistake.
Você não deveria esconder um erro.
A manager should listen carefully.
Um gerente deveria ouvir com atenção.
You should respect the deadline.
Você deveria respeitar o prazo.
You shouldn't skip the safety training.
Você não deveria pular o treinamento de segurança.
We should support the new colleague.
Nós deveríamos apoiar o novo colega.
You should set your priorities.
Você deveria definir suas prioridades.
You shouldn't speak badly about a teammate.
Você não deveria falar mal de um colega de equipe.
He should plan his career.
Ele deveria planejar a carreira.
You should give clear feedback.
Você deveria dar um retorno claro.
mistakes: You should to ask for help.
You should ask for help.
Depois de 'should' não se usa 'to'.
You should asks questions.
You should ask questions.
O verbo depois de 'should' fica na forma base, sem -s.
You not should hide a mistake.
You shouldn't hide a mistake.
A negativa é 'shouldn't' (should not).
He should respects the deadline.
He should respect the deadline.
Com he, o verbo após should não leva -s.
You shouldn't to miss the meeting.
You shouldn't miss the meeting.
Também não use 'to' após shouldn't.

celebrate.en: Great job. Clear, respectful advice is the heart of good people management — and you just practised it in English.
celebrate.pt: Ótimo trabalho. Conselhos claros e respeitosos são a base da boa gestão de pessoas — e você acabou de praticá-los em inglês.

title: Talking about what you would do
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender o Segundo Condicional para falar de situações hipotéticas: 'se acontecesse X, eu faria Y'. Em Gestão de Pessoas na Delta Ducon, isso ajuda a discutir cenários de contratação, retenção e clima organizacional que ainda não são reais.
intro: Good managers think about 'what if' situations. What if a key engineer left? What if the team grew?
Today we use the Second Conditional to talk about imaginary situations and their results. It helps you plan and reflect with your team at Delta Ducon.
introAudio: Hello, I am Diego from People Management. If I had more time, I would offer more training to my team. Let us learn to talk about these situations in English.
vocab: If turnover fell, the team would be stronger.
If we raised the salary, more people would apply.
Good retention would save training costs.
If the workload dropped, morale would rise.
If she got a promotion, she would lead the team.
practice: If we improved ______, fewer people would leave.
retention
If the ______ were fair, more candidates would apply.
salary
If the ______ were lighter, the team would feel less tired.
workload
If she got a ______, she would manage the Diadema site.
promotion
Lower ______ would help us keep our best engineers.
turnover
If ______ rose, the team would reach the goal faster.
engagement
If we offered a ______, he would stay another year.
promotion
Better ______ would keep our experienced technicians.
retention

audio.title: If I led a bigger team
audio.text: If I led a bigger team, I would organize a training every month. If the workload were lighter, my colleagues would have more time to learn. If we offered better retention, fewer engineers would leave the company. If someone got a promotion, the whole team would celebrate. If engagement were higher, our results would improve. These are the changes I would make if I had the chance.

readAloud: If I had more time, I would train the team.
If the salary were higher, more people would apply.
If she got a promotion, she would lead the site.
If turnover fell, the team would be stronger.
If engagement rose, results would improve.
fill: If I had more time, I ___ train the team.
If we ___ the salary, more people would apply.
If she got a promotion, she ___ lead the team.
If the workload ___ lighter, morale would rise.
If turnover fell, the team ___ be stronger.
If engagement ___ higher, results would improve.
If we offered training, people ___ stay longer.
If he ___ a mentor, he would grow faster.
qa: What would you do if the team grew?
If the team grew, I would give more training.
What would happen if we raised salaries?
If we raised salaries, more people would apply.
What would you change if you had more time?
If I had more time, I would coach each person.
What would she do if she got a promotion?
If she got a promotion, she would lead the site.
Would retention improve if engagement rose?
Yes, if engagement rose, retention would improve.
sentences: If I had more time, I would train the team.
If the salary were higher, more people would apply.
If she got a promotion, she would lead the site.
If turnover fell, the team would be stronger.
If engagement rose, our results would improve.
If the workload were lighter, morale would rise.
If we offered retention bonuses, fewer people would leave.
If I led a bigger team, I would organize monthly training.
grammarPoint: O Segundo Condicional fala de situações imaginárias: If + passado simples, ... would + verbo base. If I had more time, I would train the team. — Se eu tivesse mais tempo, eu treinaria a equipe. If the salary were higher, more people would apply. — Se o salário fosse maior, mais gente se candidataria.
deepDive: Use o passado simples na parte do 'if', mas com sentido de agora ou futuro imaginado. Com o verbo to be, prefira 'were' para todos os sujeitos (If I were, if she were). Na outra parte, use 'would' + verbo base. Dica: a vírgula separa as duas partes quando a frase começa com 'if'.
examples: If I had more time, I would coach the team.
Se eu tivesse mais tempo, eu treinaria a equipe.
If the salary were higher, more people would apply.
Se o salário fosse maior, mais gente se candidataria.
If she got a promotion, she would lead the site.
Se ela fosse promovida, ela lideraria a unidade.
If turnover fell, the team would be stronger.
Se a rotatividade caísse, a equipe seria mais forte.
If engagement rose, results would improve.
Se o engajamento subisse, os resultados melhorariam.
If the workload were lighter, morale would rise.
Se a carga de trabalho fosse menor, o ânimo aumentaria.
If we offered training, people would stay.
Se oferecêssemos treinamento, as pessoas ficariam.
If he had a mentor, he would grow faster.
Se ele tivesse um mentor, cresceria mais rápido.
If I were the manager, I would listen more.
Se eu fosse o gerente, eu ouviria mais.
If we hired more staff, the workload would drop.
Se contratássemos mais pessoal, a carga cairia.
mistakes: If I would have time, I would train them.
If I had time, I would train them.
Na parte do 'if' use o passado, não 'would'.
If the salary was higher, more would apply.
If the salary were higher, more would apply.
No segundo condicional prefira 'were' para todos os sujeitos.
If she got a promotion, she will lead.
If she got a promotion, she would lead.
Use 'would', não 'will', no segundo condicional.
If turnover fell, the team would to be stronger.
If turnover fell, the team would be stronger.
Depois de 'would' não se usa 'to'.
If we hired staff, the workload would dropped.
If we hired staff, the workload would drop.
Após 'would' o verbo fica na forma base.
quick: If I ___ more time, I would train them.
If she got a promotion, she ___ lead the site.
If the salary ___ higher, more would apply.
If we ___ more staff, the workload would drop.

celebrate.en: Impressive. Thinking through 'what if' scenarios is how leaders make better decisions — and now you can discuss them in English.
celebrate.pt: Impressionante. Pensar em cenários hipotéticos é como líderes tomam decisões melhores — e agora você consegue discuti-los em inglês.

title: Remembering how the team used to work
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender a usar 'used to' para falar de hábitos e situações do passado que não acontecem mais. Em Gestão de Pessoas na Delta Ducon, isso ajuda a mostrar a evolução da equipe, dos processos e da cultura ao longo dos anos.
intro: Delta Ducon has more than 25 years of history. Teams, tools and habits have changed a lot over time.
Today we use 'used to' to describe how things were in the past but are different now. It is a great way to show progress in your team's story.
introAudio: Hi, I am Elena from People Management. We used to train the team once a year, but now we do it every month. Let us learn to talk about past habits in English.
vocab: We used to follow a slower process.
The team used to do a lot of paperwork by hand.
Technicians used to work a longer shift.
We used to hold a review only once a year.
The company culture used to be very formal.
Our headcount used to be much smaller.
practice: We used to fill out a lot of ______ by hand.
paperwork
The onboarding ______ used to take three weeks.
process
Technicians used to work a longer ______ at the factory.
shift
We used to hold a performance ______ only once a year.
review
The company ______ used to be very formal.
culture
Our ______ used to be under fifty people.
headcount
Managers used to lead each ______ without software.
process
The team ______ used to feel more distant.
culture

audio.title: How things used to be
audio.text: When I joined Delta Ducon, we used to work in a very different way. We used to do all the paperwork by hand, and the process used to be slow. Managers used to give feedback only once a year. The headcount used to be small, so everyone used to know each other well. The culture used to be quite formal. Today things are faster and more open, but I like to remember how we used to work.

readAloud: We used to do the paperwork by hand.
The process used to be very slow.
Technicians used to work a longer shift.
We used to hold a review once a year.
The culture used to be very formal.
fill: We ___ to do the paperwork by hand.
The process ___ to be very slow.
Technicians used ___ work a longer shift.
We used ___ hold a review once a year.
The culture ___ to be very formal.
Our headcount used ___ be much smaller.
Managers ___ to give feedback once a year.
Everyone used ___ know each other well.
qa: How did the team use to work?
We used to do everything by hand.
Did the culture use to be formal?
Yes, it used to be very formal.
How often did you use to hold reviews?
We used to hold them once a year.
Did the team use to be smaller?
Yes, our headcount used to be under fifty.
What did managers use to do?
They used to give feedback only once a year.
sentences: We used to do the paperwork by hand.
The process used to be very slow.
Technicians used to work a longer shift.
We used to hold a review only once a year.
The culture used to be very formal.
Our headcount used to be much smaller.
Managers used to give feedback once a year.
Everyone used to know each other well.
grammarPoint: Use 'used to' + verbo base para hábitos ou situações do passado que não acontecem mais. We used to work by hand. — Nós costumávamos trabalhar à mão. The culture used to be formal. — A cultura costumava ser formal.
deepDive: 'Used to' é igual para todos os sujeitos e vem sempre com o verbo na forma base. Em perguntas e negativas, use 'did' + 'use to' (sem o -d): Did you use to work here? / We didn't use to have software. Dica: 'used to' marca contraste com o presente — antes era assim, hoje não é mais.
examples: We used to do everything by hand.
Nós costumávamos fazer tudo à mão.
The process used to be slow.
O processo costumava ser lento.
Technicians used to work a longer shift.
Os técnicos costumavam fazer um turno mais longo.
We used to hold a review once a year.
Nós costumávamos fazer uma avaliação por ano.
The culture used to be very formal.
A cultura costumava ser muito formal.
Our headcount used to be small.
Nosso número de funcionários costumava ser pequeno.
Managers used to give feedback rarely.
Os gerentes costumavam dar feedback raramente.
Everyone used to know each other.
Todos costumavam se conhecer.
I used to work at the Diadema site.
Eu costumava trabalhar na unidade de Diadema.
We didn't use to have online training.
Nós não costumávamos ter treinamento online.
mistakes: We use to do the paperwork by hand.
We used to do the paperwork by hand.
Na afirmativa é 'used to', com -d.
The process used to be slowly.
The process used to be slow.
Aqui usamos o adjetivo 'slow', não o advérbio.
We used to worked here.
We used to work here.
Depois de 'used to' o verbo fica na forma base.
Did you used to work here?
Did you use to work here?
Em perguntas com did, use 'use to', sem o -d.
We didn't used to have software.
We didn't use to have software.
Na negativa com didn't, também é 'use to', sem -d.
quick: We ___ to do the paperwork by hand.
The culture used ___ be very formal.
Technicians ___ to work a longer shift.
We used ___ hold a review once a year.
Our headcount ___ to be much smaller.

celebrate.en: Well done. Understanding how far your team has come helps you lead its future — and now you can tell that story in English.
celebrate.pt: Muito bem. Entender o quanto a equipe evoluiu ajuda você a liderar o futuro dela — e agora você sabe contar essa história em inglês.
